BURHAN:v4p426/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p426/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p426/r4.claim: In abstract or inward actions, مع marks sharing a quality, belief, or state, as in worship, truthfulness, and the prophets’ shared divine support.
BURHAN:v4p426/r4.anchor: والثاني يكثر في الأفعال المعنوية نحو آمنت مع المؤمنين وتبت مع التائبين وفهمت المسألة مع من فهمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r1.claim: God's being with the two messengers means support and aid: He hears their words and sees their deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r1.anchor: والمعية هنا بالنصرة والعون أسمع أقوالكما وأرى أفعالكما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God hears Pharaoh's reply to the messengers and sees what he does; both expressions signify knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أسمع جوابه لكما وأرى ما يفعل بكما وهما كناية عن العلم

QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r1.claim: Moses and Aaron’s admission of fear drew from God the assurance “I am with you”; their aim was to hear this promise, since prophecy should remove fear.
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r1.anchor: وكان المقصود لهما أن يقول الحق لهما : { إننى معكما }

QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r2.claim: God’s assurance calmed both men and enabled them to go to Pharaoh, since effective obligation requires that they be empowered.
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r2.anchor: سكن فيهما الخوف بقوله : { إننى معكما }

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God hears the two messengers' prayer and answers, sees what is intended against them and prevents it, so they need not worry.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أسمع دعاءكما فأجيبه، وأرى ما يراد بكما فأمنعه، لست بغافل عنكما، فلا تهتما.

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r8.claim: God's being with Moses and Aaron means supporting, protecting, and defending them, so they should deliver the message confidently despite Pharaoh's tyranny.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r8.anchor: قيل: بالنصرة والحفظ والدفع عنكما فلا تلتفتا إلى تجبره وأديا الرسالة بقوة قلب،

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r9.claim: Alternatively, God is with them through knowledge, sight, and power: He hears their speech and sees their deeds and Pharaoh's.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r9.anchor: وقيل: بالعلم والرؤية والقدرة أسمع قولكما، وقوله: وأرى فعلكما وفعله،

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains that God hears what the two will be answered and inspires them with their reply.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r10.anchor: وقيل: أسمع وأرى ما يجاوبكما به وألهمكما ما تجيبان به، عن ابن جريج.

TABRISI:20:52-53/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r16.claim: God's assurance that He is with them means He will protect and support them.
TABRISI:20:52-53/r16.anchor: بالنصرة والحفظ معناه أني ناصركما وحافظكما

TABRISI:20:52-53/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53/r17.claim: God hears what Pharaoh asks and inspires Moses and Aaron with an answer, and sees Pharaoh's intentions and wards them off.

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r1.claim: God's promise to protect Moses and Aaron resembles the statement that their enemies will not reach them.
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r1.anchor: فلا يصلون إليكما [القصص: 35]. ثم فسر سبحانه ما أجمله

THALABI:v6p246/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p246/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p246/r6.claim: God's being with Moses and Aaron means defending them; He hears both their speech and Pharaoh's and sees everyone's actions.
THALABI:v6p246/r6.anchor: قال لا تخافا إنني معكما بالدفع عنكما أسمع قولكما وقوله وأرى فعله وفعلكما

STUDYQURAN:20:45/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r5.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r5.claim: God’s assurance that He is with them means that He will protect and help Moses and Aaron.
STUDYQURAN:20:45/r5.anchor: God’s telling Moses and Aaron that He is with them is understood to mean that He will protect them and help them (Bḍ)

TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r1.claim: God tells Moses and Aaron not to fear Pharaoh because He is with them, helps them, hears their exchange, and gives them their answers.
TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r1.anchor: ما يجري بينكما وبينه، فأفهمكما ما تحاورانه به

TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r2.claim: God sees what Moses, Aaron, and Pharaoh do; none of it is hidden from Him.
TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r2.anchor: ما تفعلان ويفعل، لا يخفى علي من ذلك شيء

TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r3.speaker: حجاج
TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r3.claim: A report says God hears their conversation, reveals their response to them, and enables them to answer Pharaoh.
TAB-FULL:v16p77#2/r3.anchor: قال: ثني حجاج {قال لا تخافا إنني معكما أسمع وأرى} [طه: 46] ما يحاوركما فأوحي إليكما فتجاوبانه

TABATABAI:20:46-47/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r1.claim: God tells them not to fear Pharaoh's haste or tyranny: He is present, hears and sees, and will help rather than abandon them.
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r1.anchor: أي لا تخافا من فرطه وطغيانه إنني حاضر معكما أسمع ما يقال وأرى ما يفعل فأنصركما ولا أخذلكما

TABATABAI:20:46-47/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r2.claim: “I am with you” assures them of God's protection; hearing and seeing explain that assurance as vigilant care and aid, not mere universal presence and knowledge.
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r2.anchor: فقوله { لا تخافا } تأمين، وقوله { إنني معكما أسمع وأرى } تعليل للتأمين بالحضور والسمع والرؤية،

TABATABAI:20:46-47/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r3.claim: Some infer that hearing and seeing are attributes additional to knowledge: “I am with you” already signifies knowledge, so taking these verbs likewise would repeat it.
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r3.anchor: وقد استدل بعضهم بالآية على السمع والبصر صفتان زائدتان على العلم

TABATABAI:20:46-47/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r4.claim: The author calls this a very weak proof: “with you” means presence and witnessing, not knowledge, and certain proofs establish that God's essential attributes are identical with one another and the essence.
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r4.anchor: وأما ثانيا فلقيام البراهين اليقينية على عينية الصفات الذاتية

TABATABAI:20:46-47/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r5.claim: A speculative verbal appearance cannot override certainty; foundational doctrines must rest on knowledge, not an appeal to the default avoidance of repetition.
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r5.anchor: ولا ينعقد مع اليقين ظهور لفظي ظني مخالف البتة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r1.claim: God’s answer responds to their fear, and the promise to be with them means support, aid, and victory.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r2.claim: God’s promise to be with Moses and Aaron means support, aid, and victory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r2.anchor: {إنني معكما} وعد لهما في النصرة والمعونة والغلبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God hears their prayer and answers it, and sees what is intended against them and prevents it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (أسمع دعاءكما فأجيبه، وأرى ما يراد بكما فأمنع)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r4.claim: God is not unaware of them, so they should not be anxious.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p411/r4.anchor: والمعنى: لست بغافل عنكم فلا تهتما

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r5.claim: God is with Moses and Aaron by giving them help and victory.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r6.claim: God hears what Pharaoh says and sees what he does.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r7.claim: God reassures them Pharaoh cannot kill them before they deliver the message.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r7.anchor: {لا تخافا إنني معكما أسمع وأرى} [طه: 46] فإنه ليس بالذي يصل إلى قتلكما حتى تبلغا الرسالة.

BURHAN:v4p428/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p428/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p428/r4.claim: مع can signify aid or presence: “with you” means supporting you; God’s being with people can mean assisting them or knowing and witnessing them.

SULAMI:v1p445#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p445#5/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p445#5/r1.claim: God's being with Moses and Aaron means supporting them and observing them in every state with power, aid, and confirmation, so they need not fear delivering the message.
SULAMI:v1p445#5/r1.anchor: قال سهل : أمر الله تعالى أنه ومعهما بالنصرة . مشاهد لهما في كل حال بالقوة ، والمعونة ، والتأييد

TUSTARI:20:46/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:46/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:20:46/r1.claim: God's being with Moses and Aaron means He watches and witnesses every state, granting power, help, and support; they need not fear delivering the message.
TUSTARI:20:46/r1.anchor: أخبر الله أنه معهما بالنظر، مشاهد لكل حال هما عليه بالقوة والمعونة والتأييد، لا تخافا

SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r1.claim: The omitted objects may be 'your words' and 'your actions.'
SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r1.anchor: فقيل: تقديره: أسمع أقوالكما وأرى أفعالكما،

SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains the objects as hearing the answer given to Moses and Aaron and seeing what Pharaoh does to them.
SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أسمع جوابه لكما وأرى ما يفعل بكما،

SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r3.claim: Alternatively, the objects are omitted without specifying them, an economy ellipsis like يحْيي ويميت in 3:156.
SAMIN-DURR:20:46/r3.anchor: أو يكون من حذف الاقتصار نحو: يحيي ويميت

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r7.claim: Another possible reason for hearing before sight is its shorter range: hearing ordinarily suggests nearness, so God's promise to hear and see Moses and Aaron conveys closeness.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r7.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون تقديم السمع على البصر لسبب آخر عدا الأفضلية، وهو أن مدى السمع أقل من مدى الرؤية

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.claim: Ta-Ha presents a joint mission: both are sent, answer in fear, receive reassurance, deliver the message, and are addressed by Pharaoh together, making Aaron Moses's partner in conveying the message.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.anchor: فقد أمر كلاً من موسى وهرون بالذهاب بآياته

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r2.claim: The author favors hearing’s importance for receiving revelation: a blind person can understand a message, while a deaf person is harder to inform; prophets were not deaf, though one could be blind.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن السمع بالنسبة إلى تلقي الرسالة أفضل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r3.claim: Hearing may also precede sight because its range is shorter; in God’s assurance to Moses and Aaron, “I hear” suggests nearness, unlike seeing from afar.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p31/r3.anchor: مدى السمع أقل من مدى الرؤية فقدم ذا المدى الأقل متدرجاً من القصر إلى الطول في المدى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r3.claim: He offers another ordering rationale: hearing has shorter range than sight, so it comes first; hearing also evokes nearness, while seeing can extend farther.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r3.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون تقديم السمع على البصر لسبب آخر عدا الأفضلية وهو أن مدى السمع أقل من مدى الرؤية

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.claim: The warning إياك stands for an omitted imperative such as اتق or باعد; in the parallel warning نفسك, the suppressed verb cannot be made explicit.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.anchor: نفسك يا فلان أى اتق نفسك

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.claim: In إياك والأسد, the warned person and the accompanying الأسد are both objects; the omitted command is understood as اتق.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.claim: Other pronoun warnings likewise omit commands, including إياك إياه; a reply إياي means 'I will guard or beware of myself.'

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.claim: Because إياك is frequent, it replaces the omitted verb; paired nouns require واو, which joins the second warned object to the first.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.claim: Noun warnings such as رأسه والحائط can be understood with واو meaning مع or as ordinary coordination with an omitted command for each noun; both readings are sound Arabic.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.anchor: رأسه والحائط فالرأس مفعول معه فانتصبا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.claim: In paired warning phrases, speakers omit the verb because context and frequent use supply it; a single noun such as رأسك can instead retain an explicit imperative.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.anchor: اتق رأسك واحفظ نفسك واتق الجدار

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.claim: Verbal nouns such as الحذر الحذر and النجاء النجاء also substitute for commands, understood as الزم الحذر or عليك النجاء.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.anchor: فإنما انتصب هذا على الزم الحذر وعليك النجاء

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإذاكنتتحذرإياك|كإنكقلتإ.claim: Poetic examples by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib, al-Kumayt, and Dhū al-Iṣbaʿ confirm idiomatic warning and verbal-noun forms where an explicit verb is not used.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r1.claim: The third-person قال resumes the account and shifts from Moses’ quoted speech, framing what God answered after the two pleaded.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r1.anchor: إسناد الفعل إلى ضمير الغيبة كما قيل للاشعار بانتقال الكلام من مساق إلى مساق أخر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r2.claim: God tells them not to fear what they had mentioned about Pharaoh’s threat.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r3.claim: God’s presence means complete protection and aid; it explains the ban on fear and gives Moses and Aaron further reassurance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r3.anchor: تعليل لموجب النهى ومزيد تسلية لهما والمراد بمعيته سبحانه كمال الحفظ والنصرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r4.claim: He understands an omitted object: whatever is said and done between them and Pharaoh, allowing them to repel harm and secure good.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r4.anchor: وهو بتقدير المفعول أى ما يجرى بينكما وبينه من قول وفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r5.speaker: القفال
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r5.claim: Al-Qaffal says this answers their fear that Pharaoh would not listen or would kill them: God hears their words and sees Pharaoh’s acts, preventing what they hate.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r5.anchor: وقال القفال : يحتمل أن يكون هذا فى مقابلة القول السابق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشرى
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari estimates no object: God is protector and helper, and hearing and seeing complete the assurance; transitive verbs function intransitively.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r6.anchor: انا حافظ لكما وناصر سامع مبصر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r7.claim: Alusi finds al-Qaffal’s estimated-object account unpersuasive, while also reporting al-Zamakhshari’s objectless reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r7.anchor: فقدر المفعول أيضا لكنه كما ترى وقال الزمخشرى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r8.claim: Alusi rejects al-Tibi’s comparison with al-Mutanabbi: the verb is made intransitive here to complete the meaning of protection and aid.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r8.anchor: ويسمع واع على ما زعم الطيبى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r9.claim: The verse supports hearing and sight as attributes additional to knowledge: divine presence already implies knowledge, so this reading avoids redundancy.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p197#2/r9.anchor: واستدل بالاية على أن السمع والبصر صفتان زائدتان على العلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:46/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:46/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:46/r1.claim: God's presence with them means His protection and victory.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:46/r1.anchor: { قال لا تخافا إنني معكما } بالحفظ والنصر

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:46/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:46/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:46/r2.claim: God hears and sees everything said and done between them and Pharaoh, intervening to repel harm and grant victory; alternatively, the words describe Him as their capable, hearing, seeing protector.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:46/r2.anchor: ما يجري بينكما وبينه من قول وفعل، فأحدث في كل ما يصرف شره عنكما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r5.claim: God’s reassurance rests on His protection of His allies and destruction of His enemies; His presence is unlike kings who disappear when dispatching envoys.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r5.anchor: لا أغيب كما تغيب الملوك إذا أرسلو رسلهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r6.claim: God affirms hearing and sight: nothing about either messenger or their enemy is hidden from Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r6.anchor: لا يخفى علي شيء من حال رسولي ولا حال عدوه

DURR-FULL:v5p580/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God hears Pharaoh’s words and sees his response to the brothers, then reveals guidance so they can answer him.
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {قال لا تخافا إنني معكما أسمع وأرى} قال: أسمع ما يقول {وأرى} ما يجاوبكما فأوحي إليكما فتجاوباه

DURR-FULL:v5p580/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that when Moses asked what to say to Pharaoh, God instructed him with the phrase “Ahyā shirā hyā”; al-Aʿmash glosses it as the Living before and after all things.
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: لما بعث الله موسى إلى فرعون قال: رب أي شيء أقول قال: قل أهيا شرا هيا قال الأعمش: تفسير ذلك الحي قبل كل شيء والحي بعد كل شيء

DURR-FULL:v5p580/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports God telling Moses and Aaron not to fear Pharaoh’s clothing or power: Pharaoh cannot speak or blink except by God’s permission.
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما بعث الله موسى إلى فرعون قال: لا يغرنكما لباسه الذي ألبسته فإن ناصيته بيدي فلا ينطق ولا يطرف إلا بإذني

DURR-FULL:v5p580/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r8.claim: The same report says God could have adorned Moses and Aaron more richly than Pharaoh, but their worldly allotment would not diminish by having little of this world.
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r8.anchor: فلو شئت أن أزينكما من زينة الدنيا بشيء يعرف فرعون أن قدرته تعجز عن ذلك لفعلت وليس ذلك لهوانكما علي ولكني ألبستكما نصيبكما من الكرامة

DURR-FULL:v5p580/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r9.claim: God says He keeps His friends from worldly danger as a shepherd steers livestock from harmful places, to illuminate and purify their hearts; whoever frightens a friend of God has challenged Him, and He will avenge them on Judgment Day.
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r9.anchor: وإني لأذود أوليائي عن الدنيا كما يذود الراعي إبله عن مبارك 7 الغيرة وإني لأجنبهم كما يجنب الراعي إبله عن مراتع الهلكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r1.claim: After showing Moses the two signs, God gives him the daunting mission of confronting the earth's mightiest ruler; the next verses recount Moses and Aaron's fear and God's reassurance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r1.anchor: لما أظهر الله له الآيتين فعلم بذلك أنه مؤيد من الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r1.claim: The prohibition against fearing is an indirect assertion that neither feared outcome will occur.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r1.anchor: أي لا تخافا حصول شيء من الأمرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r2.claim: God's being with them means protective care and explains why they need not fear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r2.anchor: وجملة { إنني معكما } تعليل للنهي عن الخوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r3.claim: The verbs hear and see are treated as intransitive because their objects need not be stated: nothing escapes God's knowledge, so no feared word or act is left unguarded.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r3.anchor: ونزل فعلا { أسمع وأرى } منزلة اللازمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r4.claim: The assurance leads directly to a renewed instruction to go to Pharaoh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r4.anchor: وفرع عليه إعادة الأمر بالذهاب إلى فرعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r15.claim: God's being with Moses and Aaron means His help, protection, and power over Pharaoh, as when one says a prince is with someone to mean he protects him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r15.anchor: يريد بالنصر والمعونة والقدرة على فرعون، وهذا كما تقول الأمير مع فلان إذا أردت أنه يحميه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r16.claim: أسمع وأرى describe perception that leaves nothing hidden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r16.anchor: وأسمع وأرى عبارتان عن الإدراك الذي لا تخفى معه خافية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290/r1.claim: God's being with Moses and Aaron means His support and aid; He hears their words and sees their actions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى إنني معكما أي بالنصرة والعون أسمع أقوالكم وأرى أفعالكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290/r2.speaker: الكلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi specifies that God hears Pharaoh's reply to them and sees what Pharaoh does to them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي أسمع جوابه لكما وأرى ما يفعل بكما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r5.claim: God hears both sides and sees where they are; nothing is hidden from Him. Pharaoh's forelock is under God's control, and Pharaoh cannot speak, breathe, or strike except by permission; God protects, helps, and supports Moses and Aaron.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r5.anchor: أي: لا تخافا منه، فإنني معكما أسمع كلامكما وكلامه، وأرى مكانكما ومكانه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r6.claim: Abdullah reports that when God sent Moses to Pharaoh, Moses asked what to say; God told him “هيا شراهيا,” which al-A'mash glossed as the Living before and after everything. Ibn Kathir calls the chain good and the report unusual.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295#2/r6.anchor: عن عمرو بن مرة، عن أبي عبيدة، عن عبد الله قال: لما بعث الله عز وجل موسى إلى فرعون قال: رب، أي شيء أقول؟

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r13.claim: God's being with Moses and Aaron means protecting and guarding them, not spatial presence, since place is a bodily attribute.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r13.anchor: أنه مع العبد بالحفظ والحراسة، ولا يجوز حمله على المكان؛ لأنه من صفات الجسم

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r14.speaker: مشايخنا
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r14.claim: The author's teachers hold that hearing and seeing are attributes distinct from knowing; the Baghdadi school reduces them to knowledge.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r14.anchor: ويدل قوله: (أسمع وأرى) أنه سامع مبصر، وهما صفتان غير كونه عالما على ما يقوله مشايخنا خلاف ما تقوله البغدادية

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r15.speaker: البغدادية
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r15.claim: The Baghdadi school says hearing and seeing reduce to God's being knowing.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r15.anchor: ما يقوله مشايخنا خلاف ما تقوله البغدادية أنه يرجع إلى كونه عالما

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r16.claim: Being alive without defect is the basis of God's being hearing and seeing; actual perceiving of sensory objects is a state occasioned when those objects exist.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r16.anchor: كونه سميعا بصيرا لا لأن معناه أنه حي لا آفة به، فأما سامعا مبصرا مدركا لسائر المدركات فهي حالة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r1.claim: “With you” means God protects and supports them; hearing and seeing what happens between them and Pharaoh, He will do what protection and support require.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r1.anchor: {معكما } أي حافظكما وناصركما { أسمع وأرى } ما يجري بينكما وبينه من قول وفعل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r2.claim: The hearing and seeing may take their words and actions as explicit objects, or the verbs may stand without an expressed object, meaning that God is their watchful protector.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r2.anchor: فجائز أن يقدر أقوالكم وأفعالكم ، وجائز أن لا يقدر شيء ، وكأنه قيل : أنا حافظ لكما وناصر سامع مبصر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r3.claim: Since their protector and helper hears and sees, protection is secure and they need not fear the enemy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r3.anchor: وإذا كان الحافظ والناصر كذلك ، تم الحفظ وصحت النصرة ، وذهبت المبالاة بالعدو

MUQATIL:20:46-47/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r1.claim: God tells Moses and Aaron not to fear being killed because He is with them to defend them, as stated in 28:35.
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r1.anchor: إنني معكما } فى الدفع عنكما، فذلك قوله سبحانه: فلا يصلون إليكما

MUQATIL:20:46-47/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r2.claim: I hear means God hears Pharaoh's reply, and I see means God knows what he says.

MUQATIL:20:46-47/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r3.claim: Muqatil compares God's seeing here with the wording in 4:105, where what God shows means what He makes known.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#3/r1.claim: God's being with the two means He protects and supports them.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#3/r2.claim: God hears their words and sees their actions.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God hears their prayer and answers, and sees what is intended against them; they need not worry.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما اسمع دعاءكما فاجيبه وأرى ما يراد بكما فامتنع لست بغافل عنكما فلا تهتما

QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r1.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r1.claim: Scholars say God reassured Moses and Aaron that Pharaoh and his people would not reach them, despite their ordinary human fear.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r1.anchor: الأولى: قال العلماء: لما لحقهما ما يلحق البشر من الخوف على أنفسهما عرفهما الله سبحانه أن فرعون لا يصل إليهما

QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r2.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r2.claim: The verse refutes the claim that prophets do not fear: fearing enemies is God's way for prophets and allies despite their knowledge and trust.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r2.anchor: وهذه الآية ترد على من قال: إنه لا يخاف والخوف من الأعداء سنة الله في أنبيائه وأوليائه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī recounts ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh crossing toward water despite a lion, preferring spear wounds to God knowing he feared anything besides Him; Moses' fear answers this example.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r3.anchor: ولقد أحسن البصري رحمه الله حين قال للمخبر عن عامر بن عبد الله أنه نزل مع أصحابه في طريق الشام على ماء،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r4.claim: Moses feared when warned of a plot in Midian, watched the city anxiously, and felt fear when magicians threw ropes before God reassured him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r4.anchor: قد خاف من كان خيرا من عامر موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم حين قال له الرجل: إن الملأ يأتمرون بك

QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r5.claim: The Prophet dug the trench to protect Muslims and their property despite his unmatched trust; Companions migrated fearing persecution and torture.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r5.anchor: قلت: ومنه حفر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الخندق حول المدينة تحصينا للمسلمين وأموالهم، مع كونه من التوكل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r6.speaker: أسماء بنت عميس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r6.claim: In a report recorded by Muslim, Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays rebukes ʿUmar for claiming priority in migration, describing the Abyssinian emigrants' fear and persecution.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r6.anchor: وقد قالت أسماء بنت عميس لعمر لما قال لها سبقناكم بالهجرة، فنحن أحق برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم منكم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r7.speaker: مسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r7.claim: Qurṭubī says Muslim recorded the full report of Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays' reply.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r7.anchor: ونحن كنا نؤذى ونخاف. الحديث بطوله خرجه مسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r8.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r8.claim: Scholars say a person claiming no natural fear is lying, since people flee what harms, pains, or destroys them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r8.anchor: قال العلماء: فالمخبر عن نفسه بخلاف ما طبع الله نفوس بني آدم عليه كاذب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r9.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r9.claim: They illustrate natural fear with an unarmed person facing a ferocious lion in open country without a sword, spear, arrows, or bow.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r9.anchor: قالوا: ولا ضار أضر من سبع عاد في فلاة من الأرض على من لا آلة معه يدفعه بها عن نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r10.claim: God's being with them means support, help, and power over Pharaoh, as a prince is said to be with someone he protects.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r10.anchor: يريد بالنصر والمعونة والقدرة على فرعون. وهذا كما تقول: الأمير مع فلان إذا أردت أنه يحميه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r11.claim: I hear and see expresses awareness that leaves nothing hidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:46/r11.anchor: وقوله: { أسمع وأرى } عبارة عن الإدراك الذي لا تخفى معه خافية

BURSEVI:v5p300/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p300/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p300/r2.claim: The verb قال begins an explanatory answer to the implied question of what God said in response to their plea.
BURSEVI:v5p300/r2.anchor: {قال} استئناف بياني كأنه قيل فماذا قال لهما ربهما

BURSEVI:v5p300/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p300/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p300/r3.claim: Do not fear is consolation and a promise of protection and aid, not a command to suppress natural fear, which lies outside choice.
BURSEVI:v5p300/r3.anchor: ليس المراد منه النهي عن الخوف لأنه من حيث كونه أمرا طبيعيا

BURSEVI:v5p300/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p300/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p300/r4.claim: Fear leaves human nature through God's creative command, as when He made the fire cool and safe for Abraham.
BURSEVI:v5p300/r4.anchor: يشير إلى أن الخوف إنما يزول عن جبلة الإنسان بأمر التكوين كما قال

BURSEVI:v5p300/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p300/r5.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v5p300/r5.claim: The Mathnawī couplet presents reassurance as nourishment for the fearful: those who fear are made safe, while the person without fear does not need the lesson not to fear.
BURSEVI:v5p300/r5.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : لا تخافوا هست نزل خائفان هست درخور

BURSEVI:v5p300/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p300/r6.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v5p300/r6.claim: I am with you means complete protection and victory, not spatial proximity, since God is transcendent beyond physical location.
BURSEVI:v5p300/r6.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في "حواشيه" : ليس المراد منه النهي عن الخوف

BURSEVI:v5p300/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p300/r7.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v5p300/r7.claim: God hears and sees what happens between them and Pharaoh, and acts to repel harm and bring benefit; one accompanied by God is protected from every tyrant.
BURSEVI:v5p300/r7.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في "حواشيه" : ليس المراد منه النهي عن الخوف

BURSEVI:v5p300/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p300/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p300/r8.claim: A young preacher imprisoned by al-Rashīd in a sealed room later appeared in a garden; he said the one who put him there had also brought him out, and the caliph wept and honored him.
BURSEVI:v5p300/r8.anchor: روي أن شابا كان يأمر وينهى فحبسه الرشيد في بيت

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r7.claim: “Do not fear” addresses their two stated fears of rash punishment and transgression; it does not promise they will avoid rejection or opposition to their signs.
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r7.anchor: المراد لا تخافا مما عرض في قلبكما من الإفراط والطغيان لأن ذلك هو المفهوم من الكلام يبين ذلك أنه تعالى لم يؤمنهما من الرد

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r8.claim: God’s being “with” them means guarding and preserving them; the phrase is also used idiomatically as a prayer for someone.
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r8.anchor: فهو عبارة عن الحراسة والحفظ وعلى هذا الوجه يقال : الله معك على وجه الدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r9.claim: Hearing and seeing clarify that God’s protection includes knowledge of everything that happens to them, unlike a guardian who may not know every harm.
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r9.anchor: أكد ذلك بقوله : { أسمع وأرى } فإن من يكون مع الغير

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r10.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r10.claim: Al-Qaffāl pairs hearing with Pharaoh’s rushing ahead by not listening to them, and seeing with his transgression by killing them; God will hear their words and prevent the feared outcome.
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r10.anchor: قال القفال قوله : { أسمع وأرى } يحتمل أن يكون مقابلا لقوله : { أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى } والمعنى

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r11.claim: Because “I am with you” already denotes knowledge, the added “I hear and see” indicates hearing and sight are attributes additional to knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r11.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أن كونه تعالى سميعا وبصيرا صفتان زائدتان على العلم لأن قوله : { إننى معكما } دل على العلم
